This question evaluates end-to-end system design for multilingual, real-time sarcasm detection with code-switching support, drift control, weak supervision capabilities, and privacy-by-design principles.

- **Streaming architectures and latency budgeting**: Processing messages in real-time with minimal delay

- **Weak supervision labeling**: Leveraging heuristic or noisy labels to train models without exhaustive manual annotation
- **Privacy-by-design**: Minimizing data collection and ensuring user privacy throughout the pipeline
- **Safe rollback mechanisms**: Implementing safeguards to revert to previous model versions when performance degrades

## Why This Is Asked

- Text normalization: emoji/slang handling
- Lightweight bilingual features; on-device constraints
- Hybrid rule+ML approach; latency and privacy trade-offs

## Code Example

import re
EMOJI_MAP = {":)": "smile"}
def normalize(text):
  for k,v in EMOJI_MAP.items():
    text = text.replace(k, v)
  text = re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", "", text)
  return text.lower()
```

def infer_stream(batch):

    if scores.max() < low_thresh[lang]:

    return label, scores.max()
```
